findings.explanation: Splunkbase 4856 is the community 'Metrics Add-on for Infrastructure' and 1810 (cited for Splunk_TA_vmware) is 'Hunk App for MongoDB'. The VMware NSX-T Splunk App is 4241 and the Splunk Add-on for VMware is 3215. The wrong IDs repeat in dataSources, detailedImplementation and references, and the repository guide makes the same error.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Splunkbase 4241 for the NSX-T app and 3215 for Splunk_TA_vmware everywhere, and correct docs/guides/datacenter-fabric-sdn.md.

findings.explanation: The NSX API reference documents GET /api/v1/cluster/status, GET /api/v1/cluster/nodes and GET /api/v1/cluster/nodes/{node-id}/status, and per-node services under /api/v1/cluster/{cluster-node-id}/node/services/... . I found no /policy/api/v1/cluster/* variants, no 'runtime/info' path and no /cluster/nodes/<id>/services/<svc>/status path. The same list repeats in detailedImplementation Step 1 and in the implementation quick win.
findings.suggested_fix: Check each path in the NSX 4.2 API reference and replace it with the documented /api/v1/cluster/status, /api/v1/cluster/nodes/{node-id}/status and /api/v1/cluster/{node-id}/node/services/{service}/status routes.

findings.explanation: The Async Replicator (ASYNC_REPLICATOR group) is the NSX Federation GM-to-LM replication service. Its documented health checks are service status (GET /api/v1/node/services/async_replicator/status) and sync alarms, not a lag-in-seconds metric. The aggregation-service statistics endpoint and the claim that it yields ARS lag could not be confirmed, so asr_lag_seconds (the main numeric threshold) may have no real source.
findings.quote: Capture **GET /api/v1/aggregation-service/cluster-statistics** payloads so Aggregation backlog proxies flatten into numeric **asr_lag_seconds** columns
findings.suggested_fix: Name a documented source for replication lag (for example the Federation GM–LM sync status API) or drop the lag thresholds. Also state that ARS applies only to NSX Federation deployments.

findings.explanation: NSX cluster group status is reported as STABLE, DEGRADED or UNAVAILABLE (members UP/DOWN). DATASTORE (Corfu) becomes UNAVAILABLE when two of three members are down. LOST_QUORUM and NO_QUORUM are not NSX values, and the SPL never checks UNAVAILABLE, so a real quorum loss would not match.
findings.quote: Quorum loss: correlate DOWN or LOST_QUORUM strings with counts of healthy nodes
findings.suggested_fix: Describe quorum loss as the DATASTORE group (or overall mgmt_cluster_status) reporting UNAVAILABLE, and request an SPL change to match STABLE/DEGRADED/UNAVAILABLE.

findings.explanation: This contradicts the 'least-privilege identities' prerequisite in the same field and the grounding guide, which says the read-only Auditor role is enough for collectors.
findings.quote: Collector identities often possess Enterprise Admin scopes
findings.suggested_fix: Tell readers to use the NSX Auditor role for collectors and never Enterprise Admin.

findings.explanation: 'set cluster restore' is not a documented NSX CLI command. Recovery from loss of quorum is normally done with 'deactivate cluster' on the surviving node, followed by re-deploying members. The 'five-second' heartbeat claim and the 'etcd_status' field (NSX uses Corfu, not etcd) are also unsupported.
findings.quote: Follow Manager cluster restore workflows referencing **set cluster restore**
findings.suggested_fix: Check the NSX 4.2 'Recover from loss of quorum' procedure and quote the real CLI. Remove etcd_status and the heartbeat figure unless a source is cited.

findings.explanation: The SPL's real triggers are cluster status DOWN/DEGRADED/UNKNOWN, asr_pk > 90, vip_moves > 0, service splits or quorum hints. 'asr_lag_seconds > 60' applies only together with a non-UP cluster, and ars_hot (> 120) no longer exists after stats, so it never fires. The prose turns three overlapping lag numbers into an OR list. The same list appears in controlTest.
findings.suggested_fix: List the actual output conditions from the final where clause in plain words, with one lag threshold.

findings.explanation: The SPL aggregates by cluster_id and _time only and outputs no node_id, so no per-node matrix can be built from it. Panel 4 also charts corfu_layout_state 'versions', which the SPL upper-cases as a string.
findings.quote: (2) Matrix panel of Manager vs Policy vs Search vs CCP status tiles keyed by node_id.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe panels the SPL output supports (per-cluster status tiles), or note that a separate per-node search is needed.

findings.explanation: Microsoft 365 has nothing to do with NSX Manager cluster health, and PagerDuty is only an alert destination, not a monitored system.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove m365 and pagerduty from equipment.

findings.explanation: Cluster-group health and replication status fit neither the CIM Performance datasets (CPU, Memory, Storage, Network, OS) nor Inventory well, and the SPL uses no datamodel.
findings.suggested_fix: Leave cimModels empty (raw NSX REST data), or keep Inventory only if Manager nodes are actually mapped as inventory entities.

findings.explanation: The text uses jargon (NSX Manager, VIP) and puzzling metaphors that a non-technical reader cannot decode. The UC also watches a three-node cluster of appliances, not a 'trio folded into each box'.
findings.quote: We mind the trio folded into each NSX Manager box—intent ledger, policy planner, fast finder—and whether their shared journal stays mirrored plus who fronts the VIP.
findings.suggested_fix: Say plainly: 'NSX's control software runs on three cooperating servers. We check that they stay in agreement, that their shared records stay in sync, and that the front-door address does not keep jumping between them, and we warn the team before network changes stop working.'

findings.explanation: The reviewer is an agent, the add-on IDs are wrong, the API paths are unconfirmed and the SPL has parse errors. There is no evidence of SME validation.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft until an NSX SME has validated the collectors and the search.

findings.explanation: The link goes to the generic NSX 4.2 landing page, not a Corfu page. A second reference points to the Broadcom techdocs root, which helps no one.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the NSX 4.2 'Troubleshoot NSX Manager Cluster' / cluster status API pages instead.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The base search uses match(lower(_raw), ...) before the first pipe. The search command does not evaluate eval functions, so the syslog branch does not filter as written.

quorum_hint=case(..., null()) and svc_split=case(..., null()) end with a lone null() and so have an odd number of arguments. case() needs condition/value pairs, so the eval fails. Drop the trailing null(), since case() already returns null when nothing matches.

streamstats window=3 latest(vip_owner) runs with the default current=t, so vip_prev includes the current event and equals vip_owner, and vip_flap is effectively always 0. The preceding sort by cluster_id node_id _time also interleaves nodes, so even with current=f the comparison would mix different nodes' views.

Status matching uses UP/DOWN/LOST_QUORUM/NO_QUORUM, but NSX cluster groups report STABLE/DEGRADED/UNAVAILABLE. UNAVAILABLE, the real quorum-loss value, is never matched. ars_hot is referenced after stats but is not carried through, so that condition never fires.
T1499.004 (Endpoint DoS: Application or System Exploitation) does not fit a management-plane health UC. The SPL detects no adversary behaviour, so the tag overclaims security coverage.

summary: The UC targets a real need (NSX Manager cluster group health, VIP ownership, Corfu quorum). However, the Splunkbase IDs are wrong, several API paths and fields (Policy-prefixed cluster status, runtime/info, ARS lag seconds, aggregation-service statistics) do not match the documented NSX API, and the SPL has parse and logic errors. It also expects UP/DOWN/LOST_QUORUM status strings that NSX does not emit.
